Reason : The drift velocity of electron in presence of electric field decreases.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: In the absence of external electric field, the free electrons move randomly in the conductor, so their drift velocity is zero and therefore there is no current in the conductor. In the presence of electric field, each electron in the conductor experiences a force in a direction opposite to the electric field. Now the free electrons are drifted from negative end to the positive end of the conductor and hence a current starts to flow in the conductor.

questions.q: An electric bulb marked $40 \mathrm{~W}$ and $200 \mathrm{~V}$, is used in a circuit of supply voltage $100 \mathrm{~V}$. Now its power is
questions.solution:
Actual power of bulb $\left(P_1\right)=40 \mathrm{~W}$ Actual voltage of bulb $\left(V_1\right)=200 \mathrm{~V}$ and supply voltage $\left(V_2\right)=100 \mathrm{~V}$
Power $(P)=\frac{V^2}{R} \propto V^2$. Therefore $\frac{P_1}{P_2}=\frac{V_1^2}{V_2^2}$ or, $\frac{40}{P_2}=\frac{(200)^2}{(100)^2}=4$ or $P_2=\frac{40}{4}=10 \mathrm{~W}$
(where $P_2=$ power when voltage is $100 \mathrm{~V}$ ).
